learn.hook: More than 2500 years ago, the Indian mathematician Baudhayana wrote down a rule for building fire altars that we still use to find distances today!
points: A right triangle has one angle of 90°. The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, and it is the longest side.
The Baudhayana–Pythagoras theorem: if the legs are a and b and the hypotenuse is c, then a² + b² = c².
In Baudhayana's words (roughly): the diagonal of a rectangle makes a square as big as the squares on its length and breadth put together.
To find the hypotenuse: c = √(a² + b²). To find a leg: a = √(c² − b²).
Converse: if the sides of a triangle satisfy a² + b² = c², then the angle opposite c is a right angle.

example.q: A 13 m ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
steps: The ladder is the hypotenuse: c = 13
One leg is 5, let the height be h

learn.reallife: Firefighters placing ladders, TV makers measuring screen size along the diagonal, and pilots finding straight-line distances all use this theorem.

items.text: In a right triangle, the longest side is called the ___
If the legs are 6 and 8, then hypotenuse² = ___
The hypotenuse is opposite the ___ angle
If c² = a² + b², the angle opposite c is ___

quiz.q: The two shorter sides of a right triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides (14) instead of their squares, or forgets the square root (100)

quiz.q: A 13 m ladder leans on a wall with its foot 5 m away from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
quiz.explain: The ladder is the hypotenuse. Height² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the height is 12 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the squares instead of subtracting, or forgets the square root

quiz.q: Which side of a right triangle is always the longest?
options: Any side can be the longest
quiz.explain: c² = a² + b² is bigger than a² and bigger than b², so c is longer than both legs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the side drawn at the bottom (base) is always the longest

quiz.q: Riya walks 9 m east and then 12 m north. How far is she from her starting point in a straight line?
quiz.explain: East and north make a right angle. Distance² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, so the distance is 15 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two distances walked (21 m)

quiz.q: A TV screen is 80 cm wide and 60 cm tall. How long is its diagonal?
quiz.explain: Diagonal² = 80² + 60² = 6400 + 3600 = 10,000, so the diagonal is 100 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the width and height instead of using squares

quiz.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 25 cm and one leg of 24 cm. How long is the other leg?
quiz.explain: Other leg² = 25² − 24² = 625 − 576 = 49, so it is 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the sides (25 − 24 = 1) instead of their squares

quiz.q: The squares on the two legs of a right triangle have areas 36 cm² and 64 cm². What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
quiz.explain: The theorem says the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the legs: 36 + 64 = 100 cm².
quiz.mistake: Gives the side length (10) instead of the area, or subtracts

quiz.q: In triangle PQR, ∠Q = 90°. Which equation is correct?
quiz.explain: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle at Q, so it is PR. Then PR² = PQ² + QR².
quiz.mistake: Does not find the side opposite the right angle first

teach.ask: Gappu asks: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. How do I find the long side?
teach.praise: Square the legs: 9 and 16. Add: 25. Square root: 5! Baudhayana would be proud!
teach.nudge: What do you do to 3 and 4 first? And after adding, how do you get back to a length?

learn.hook: 3, 4, 5 is a magic trio: 9 + 16 = 25. Are there more such trios? Infinitely many!
points: A Pythagorean triple is three whole numbers a, b, c with a² + b² = c². The smallest is (3, 4, 5).
Multiply a triple by any whole number to get another: (6, 8, 10), (9, 12, 15), (30, 40, 50).
Some triples are not multiples of smaller ones: (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), (20, 21, 29).
A recipe: for any whole number m > 1, the numbers 2m, m² − 1 and m² + 1 form a triple. For m = 4: 8, 15, 17.
To test a triple, square the two smaller numbers, add them, and compare with the square of the largest.
learn.reallife: Carpenters and tile layers use triples like 6-8-10 to check that corners are truly square.

quiz.q: Which of these is a Pythagorean triple?
quiz.mistake: Picks numbers that just look close together

quiz.q: Complete the Pythagorean triple (9, 40, __).
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 and 40 instead of their squares

quiz.q: Using 2m, m² − 1 and m² + 1 with m = 7, what is the largest number of the triple?
quiz.mistake: Uses m² (49) without adding 1

quiz.q: (3, 4, 5) is a triple. Which of these is also a triple made by multiplying it?
quiz.explain: (15, 20, 25) = 5 × (3, 4, 5). Multiplying every number by the same amount keeps a² + b² = c².
quiz.mistake: Adds the same number to each, or multiplies only some of the numbers

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 10 cm and 24 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
quiz.mistake: Uses the triple (5, 12, 13) but forgets to double 13

quiz.q: Harpreet's triangle has sides 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm. Is it a right triangle?
options: Yes, because 25 is the longest side
quiz.explain: 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². By the converse of the theorem, the triangle has a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides instead of their squares

quiz.q: In the Pythagorean triple (20, 21, x), what is x?
How many Pythagorean triples are there?
quiz.explain: Multiplying (3, 4, 5) by 2, 3, 4, ... gives a new triple every time, and that never ends.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only the few famous triples exist

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I check if 5, 12, 13 is a Pythagorean triple?
teach.praise: 25 + 144 = 169 = 13². The two small squares add up to the big square. It is a triple!
teach.nudge: What do you do with 5 and 12? Then what do you compare the answer with?

topics.title: Proof ideas and using the converse

learn.hook: Can you prove a² + b² = c² with just four paper triangles and a square? Yes, with a cut-and-arrange trick!
points: Area proof: draw a big square of side (a + b). Put 4 copies of the right triangle in its corners. The space left in the middle is a tilted square of side c.
Big square area = 4 triangles + middle square: (a + b)² = 4 × ½ab + c². So a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c², which gives a² + b² = c².
Rearrangement: slide the same 4 triangles into a different position in the big square, and the space left is two squares, a² and b². Same leftover area, so a² + b² = c².
Baudhayana used the diagonal to double a square: the square on the diagonal of a square has twice its area.
Converse in action: if the longest side c gives a² + b² = c², the triangle is right-angled. If a² + b² > c² it is acute; if a² + b² < c² it is obtuse.

example.q: Use the area proof with a = 3 and b = 4 to find c.

learn.reallife: Masons mark a perfect right angle for a house corner with a knotted rope stretched into a 3-4-5 triangle.

games.title: Build the proof
games.prompt: Put the steps of the area proof in order
items: Draw a big square of side a + b
Place four copies of the right triangle in its corners
The middle space is a tilted square of side c
Big square = 4 triangles + middle square: (a + b)² = 2ab + c²
Expand: a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c², so a² + b² = c²

games.title: Right or not?
items: A triangle with sides 6, 8 and 10 has a right angle.
A triangle with sides 4, 5 and 6 has a right angle.
16 + 25 = 41, but 6² = 36. It is an acute triangle.
The diagonal of a square with side 1 has length √2.
In every triangle, a² + b² = c².
This is true only for right triangles.
A knotted rope with sides 3, 4 and 5 units can be used to mark a right angle.
3² + 4² = 5², so by the converse the angle between 3 and 4 is 90°.
If both legs of a right triangle are doubled, the hypotenuse also doubles.

quiz.q: In the area proof, a big square of side (a + b) holds 4 right triangles with legs a and b, and a middle square of side c. If a = 3 and b = 4, what is the area of the middle square?
quiz.explain: Big square = 7² = 49. Four triangles = 4 × 6 = 24. Middle square = 49 − 24 = 25, so c = 5.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract the triangles, or uses only one triangle

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
quiz.explain: 5² + 6² = 61, which is less than 8² = 64. When the two smaller squares add to less than the largest square, the triangle is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any triangle with whole-number sides is right-angled

quiz.q: What is the diagonal of a square of side 5 cm? (Use √2 ≈ 1.41.)
quiz.mistake: Adds the two sides (10 cm) instead of using the theorem

quiz.q: Baudhayana's idea: a square is drawn on the diagonal of a square of side 6 cm. What is the area of the new square?
quiz.explain: Diagonal² = 6² + 6² = 72. The new square's area is diagonal², which is 72 cm², twice the original 36 cm².
quiz.mistake: Doubles the side (12 cm), which makes 144 cm², four times the area

quiz.q: Why do masons use a knotted rope with sides 3, 4 and 5 units?
options: Because 3² + 4² = 5², so the triangle has a right angle for making square corners
Because it makes an equilateral triangle
Because ropes cannot make other shapes
quiz.explain: By the converse of the theorem, sides 3, 4, 5 must make a right angle between the 3 and 4 sides.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the converse of the theorem to real right angles

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 9, 10 and 12. Is it acute, right or obtuse?
quiz.explain: 9² + 10² = 181, which is more than 12² = 144. When the two smaller squares add to more than the largest, all angles are acute.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which way the inequality points to acute or obtuse

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12. If both legs are doubled, what is the new hypotenuse?
quiz.explain: The old hypotenuse is 13. Doubling both legs doubles the hypotenuse: 26. Check: 10² + 24² = 676 = 26².
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hypotenuse stays the same or becomes 4 times bigger

quiz.q: In the rearrangement proof, the four triangles are moved inside the same big square so that two squares are left uncovered. What are their areas?
quiz.explain: The leftover space is a square of side a and a square of side b. Before the move it was one square of side c, so a² + b² = c².
quiz.mistake: Confuses the triangles' areas (½ab) with the leftover squares

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How does putting 4 triangles inside a big square prove a² + b² = c²?
teach.praise: The leftover space is c² in one arrangement and a² + b² in the other. Same space, so they are equal. Mind blown!
teach.nudge: What is left uncovered in the middle? And what is left after you move the triangles?
